title: MedDiTPro: A Prompt-Guided Diffusion Transformer for Multimodal Longitudinal Medical Data Synthesis

problem.claim: Synthetic EHR generation must preserve multimodal, fine-grained code-level, intra-visit, and inter-visit temporal structure.

gap.claim: Existing diffusion methods have limited modality-aware representation learning and adaptability, while evaluation paradigms do not robustly assess intra-visit code relationships and inter-visit temporal patterns.

contributions.claim: MedDiTPro is a diffusion transformer-based framework that integrates structured modality-aware guidance for multimodal EHR generation.
The framework combines a unified transformer for intra-visit representation learning, a modality-specific and datawise prompt learner, and a structured-guidance diffusion transformer.
The framework evaluates synthetic records across fidelity, privacy preservation, and utility on publicly available datasets.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report state-of-the-art performance for generating diverse and clinically meaningful synthetic records.
The authors report state-of-the-art fidelity, privacy preservation, and utility on publicly available datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: Diffusion models are presented as a state-of-the-art approach for synthetic EHR generation.
Existing methods and evaluation paradigms are described as inadequate for multimodal dependencies, code-level interactions, heterogeneous EHR structure, and longitudinal patterns.
The authors propose MedDiTPro with structured modality-aware guidance.
MedDiTPro uses unified transformer representations, modality-specific and datawise prompts, and a structured-guidance diffusion transformer.
Experiments on publicly available datasets are reported to achieve state-of-the-art fidelity, privacy preservation, and utility.

source_observation.claim: The proposed framework combines modality-aware guidance with transformer-based representation learning for multimodal EHR synthesis.

interpretation.claim: Explicitly modeling modality interactions may address limitations that arise when heterogeneous medical data are handled without structured guidance.

application.claim: Multimodal synthesis systems may benefit from modality-specific prompts and shared representations when inputs contain heterogeneous and evolving data types.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these design choices improve performance independently or generalize beyond the reported EHR datasets.

unknowns: The specific publicly available datasets are not identified.
Quantitative results, baselines, and evaluation metrics are not provided.
The privacy-preservation procedure and threat model are not described.
Clinical meaningfulness and utility validation procedures are not specified.
